title: Schemas package: phax's persisted formats as a typed npm package

ground.note: 'Spec candidates' → 'Three additive specs…' item 3 (schemas-package: persisted-format schemas published alone, freezing nothing beyond the 1.0 promise, typed parsing for a read-only records consumer); 'Road to 1.0.0' → the persisted-format stability promise (phax.json, run status files, approvals.json, phax/records/v1) is a 1.0 blocker not yet written; 'Library readiness' → the app/ports library API waits for 1.0.

42 Effect Schema modules. The persisted formats a third party reads are registry.ts, status.ts (run and phase status), phaxPlan.ts, complianceReview.ts, approvalRecord.ts, specApprovalRecord.ts, runRecord.ts (phase record manifest, version 2), authoringRecord.ts (authoring record plus the record-manifest union), specDocument.ts and planDocument.ts. The rest are internal: provider output streams, config layers, gate and reconciliation documents, session bindings, the extraction cache, orient, plan-audit, scopes, telemetry events.

The schema modules reach outside src/schemas in two places: status.ts imports BranchNameSchema from domain/branded.ts, which is pure and uses only effect, and runRecord.ts imports SurfaceSchema from phaxConfig.ts. vibeOutput.ts imports node:fs, so it must stay out of any published closure.
Most decoders reject excess properties (onExcessProperty: error), but registry.ts and status.ts use the default and ignore them. Parity has to follow each format's own setting.
The records branch is phax/records/v1. A manifest is record.json, keyed <runId>/<phaseId> for a phase or authoring/<authoringId> for an authoring session, beside an optional output.jsonl.

The root package is 'phax', built with tsc -p tsconfig.build.json to dist/ with declarations. src/ is ESM and uses node: built-ins and npm dependencies only. Its only runtime dependency relevant to schemas is effect ^3.14.0.
The package published to npm, @lbdremy/phax, is only a launcher: bin/phax plus a binary resolver. The release workflow sets its version to match the tag. The tsc output is published nowhere.
Deno is used only to smoke-test and cross-compile the four release binaries.

On a tag, the workflow runs the gate, builds the binaries, version-matches npm/package.json and runs npm stage publish --provenance for one package; a maintainer approves the staged package by hand. release.sh bumps package.json and npm/package.json in one release commit.
Three formats sit outside the 'version: 1 stability promise that covers phax.json and the run formats': spec document, plan document and authoring record.
Draft. It introduces code-review.json, pass.json and the review-plan document, all shipped experimental.

Not readable in this session (permission denied). The consumer's need is taken from the brief (item 0.9): a read-only cockpit reads records with these types and never with a hand-written parser, and a docs pipeline renders JSON Schemas as reference pages.

Walked 2026-09-28 across every commit of phax/records/v1 (each commit carries its own tree): 6 phase records at version 1 and 51 at version 2; 8 authoring records at version 1, of which 2 lack sourceSha — an experimental format changed shape without a version bump. docs/specs/approvals.json and docs/plans/approvals.json: version 1 with one record shape across all 84 commits that touched them.

context: phax writes its state as JSON documents that other tools can read later. The run registry lives at ~/.phax/registry.json. Each run directory holds run-status.json, a status.json per phase, phax-plan.json and, after a review, compliance-review.json. The repo holds the plan and spec approval files (docs/plans/approvals.json, docs/specs/approvals.json). The phax/records/v1 branch holds record manifests: <runId>/<phaseId>/record.json for a phase and authoring/<authoringId>/record.json for a headless authoring session. Since 0.16.0, headless authoring also writes a JSON sidecar beside each spec and plan it authors. phax decodes every one of these with an Effect Schema in src/schemas. That directory also holds many purely internal schemas: provider output streams, config layers, gate diagnostics and attribution, reconciliation, session bindings, the extraction cache, and orient and plan-audit responses. Four schemas are already rendered to JSON Schema: phax.json through phax schema upgrade, phax-plan, and the spec and plan documents through phax artifact schema spec|plan. phax builds with tsc to dist/ with declarations. src/ uses node: built-ins and npm dependencies and no Deno API; Deno only compiles the four release binaries. The npm package, @lbdremy/phax, is a launcher for those binaries. It is version-matched to the tag, staged with npm stage publish --provenance and approved by hand. The tsc output itself is published nowhere. The README names three experimental formats outside the 'version: 1' promise. NEXT_STEPS lists the persisted-format promise as a 1.0 blocker that is still to be written. The first consumer is the steme roadmap-1.0 experiment: a read-only cockpit that reads records with phax's types, and a docs pipeline that renders each format's JSON Schema as a reference page.
problem: Today a tool that wants to read what phax wrote has two options, and both are wrong. The first is to write its own parser from phax's source. That creates a second decoder that drifts silently the first time phax bumps a format (the phase record manifest is already at version 2 and gained verifiedSurfaces in 0.10), and it will accept and reject documents differently from phax. The second is to depend on phax's source tree. That pulls in the CLI, the adapters and every internal schema, and says nothing about which formats are safe to depend on. Neither option gives the cockpit typed reads or gives the docs pipeline a JSON Schema per format. Neither can read the history: a document an older phax wrote is rejected, or read by a guess. There is also a risk on the other side. Publishing every schema in src/schemas as public API would freeze internal formats that the 1.0 promise never covered.

productGoal.statement: Publish phax's persisted-format decoders as a small, standalone, typed npm package, released at the same version as phax. The package ships the schemas phax actually uses, not a copy. A third-party reader then gets the same accept or reject verdict phax would give on any document, a TypeScript type for the decoded value, and a JSON Schema for its docs. Every document phax has ever written stays readable, whatever release wrote it; a format is not stable or experimental, it has shapes.
productGoal.guidingRule: The package is phax's own decoder, published: it accepts exactly what phax accepts, exports every format phax persists and nothing internal, and reads every shape phax has ever written.

terminology.definition: A JSON document that phax writes and that a third party can read later. It is identified by its `$schema`: the format id and the phax release that wrote it. A pre-schema document, written before `$schema`, is identified by where it lives, for example run-status.json.
The npm package @lbdremy/phax-schemas described by this spec.
The package's import path, `@lbdremy/phax-schemas`, which carries every persisted format, plus the `json/` directory of JSON Schemas. There is no second entry.
A schemas-package function that takes an already-JSON-parsed value of unknown type and returns a Parsed result. The result is either the typed value or a failure with a path and a message.

A parse function has parity when it gives the same accept or reject verdict as phax's own decoder for that format on every document, including how it treats unknown keys. Parity holds for the version phax currently writes; older shapes are read by historical decoders phax no longer carries.

The `record.json` at the root of a record: its index card (run, phase, model, outcome, usage, verified surfaces). Two kinds: the phase record manifest (format id `phase-record-manifest`) and the authoring record manifest (`authoring-record-manifest`, kind "authoring").
The schemas package's version always equals the version of the phax release whose tag produced it.

The stable name of a persisted format, independent of any file name or location: registry, run-status, phase-status, phax-plan, compliance-review, plan-approvals, spec-approvals, phase-record-manifest, authoring-record-manifest, gate-attribution, phase-file-reconciliation, gate-diagnostics, gate-pending, spec-document, plan-document, code-review.

The `$schema` value phax writes as the first key of every document: `https://docs.phax.run/schemas/<format id>/<release>.json`. It names the format and the release that wrote the document, and it is the only version marker a new document carries.

The decoder of a shape phax no longer writes: a format's pre-schema shape, and every released shape since. It lives in the package, one module per shape, and is never modified after the release that froze it.

The committed JSON Schema of one shape, stored as `<format id>/<shape release>.schema.json`, or `<format id>/pre-schema.schema.json`. A shape not yet released is `<format id>/next.schema.json`, renamed to the release version by `release.sh`. The latest snapshot of a format must equal the schema generated from phax's decoder.

One JSON shape of a format. A shape is named by the release that first wrote it (its shape release). Each format has one earlier shape, `pre-schema`: exactly the shape phax writes until the first release that writes `$schema`. A document written by release X has the latest shape released at or before X.

A document written before the first release that writes `$schema`. It carries a `version` literal (or, for the timeline files, none) and is identified by where it lives. It is read by the frozen decoder of its format's pre-schema shape, or reported unsupported.

The version in phax's root `package.json`. phax writes it in `$schema`; a development build therefore names the last cut release, and its documents are not meant to be read before a release names their shape.

A folder on phax/records/v1 for one phase (`<runId>/<phaseId>/`) or one headless authoring session (`authoring/<authoringId>/`). It holds the record manifest and the files the phase produced: the diff, the gate logs, `gate-attribution.json`, `file-reconciliation.json`, the gate diagnostics and pending documents, the handoff, the transcript, and technical files. "Record" always means the folder, never one file.

The first phax release that writes `$schema`. Every document written from that release on stays readable forever; a document written before it is read only if its format's pre-schema decoder accepts it.

requirements.title: Standalone package
requirements.statement: The system shall publish its persisted-format schemas as a standalone npm package, @lbdremy/phax-schemas, that installs and imports without the phax CLI, its binaries or its source tree.

requirements.title: Runtime dependencies
requirements.statement: The schemas package shall declare effect as its only runtime dependency.

requirements.title: No side effects
requirements.statement: The schemas package shall contain no code that reads files, spawns processes, opens network connections or references a node: or Deno built-in.

requirements.title: Every persisted format on one entry
requirements.statement: The schemas package's entry shall export a schema, a TypeScript type and a parse function for exactly these formats: run registry, run status, phase status, phax-plan, compliance review, plan approvals, spec approvals, spec document, plan document; from a record, the phase record manifest, the authoring record manifest, the record-manifest union, the gate attribution, the phase file reconciliation, the gate diagnostics document and the gate pending document.

requirements.title: A record's timeline files are read like any format
requirements.statement: The schemas package shall read the files a record carries for a phase's timeline — its manifest, `gate-attribution.json`, `file-reconciliation.json`, and each gate attempt's diagnostics and pending documents — each with its own parse function, so a reader rebuilds a phase's gate, fix loops and reconciliation without a parser of its own.

requirements.title: Nothing internal
requirements.statement: The schemas package shall export no internal schema and no module of phax's app, ports, infra or cli layers. Internal schemas are provider output streams (a record's transcript), config layers (phax.json and the user overlay), the global reconciliation, session and agent-binding documents, model resolution, security posture, the extraction cache, and orient and plan-audit responses.

requirements.title: Same verdict as phax
requirements.statement: WHEN a schemas-package parse function is given a document of the shape phax currently writes THE schemas package SHALL accept it if and only if phax's own decoder for that format accepts it.

requirements.title: Failures are values
requirements.statement: IF a document fails to parse THEN the parse function SHALL return a failure carrying the path and message of the first violation, without throwing.

requirements.title: Every version ever written is readable
requirements.statement: WHEN a parse function is given a document THE schemas package SHALL decode it with the decoder of its shape — for a document carrying `$schema`, the latest shape released at or before the release it names; for a pre-schema document, its format's pre-schema shape — and return its exact shape with the shape's id.

requirements.title: Older than the pre-schema shape is unsupported
requirements.statement: IF a pre-schema document is rejected by its format's pre-schema decoder THEN the parse function SHALL return a failure stating that the document is older than the first supported release and naming that release, without throwing and without trying any older shape.

requirements.title: Tests use no real documents
requirements.statement: The schemas package's tests shall build their documents from the schemas themselves or write them by hand; no document copied from a phax home, a records branch or another repository's history shall be committed.

requirements.title: A document is identified by itself
requirements.statement: WHEN `parseDocument` is given a document carrying `$schema` THE schemas package SHALL identify its format from `$schema` alone, whatever the file's name or location, and return the format id, the shape id and the parsed value.

requirements.title: A newer version is named, not guessed
requirements.statement: IF a document's `$schema` names a release newer than the package, or a format id the package does not know, THEN the parse function SHALL return a failure naming the URL and the package version, and stating that the package must be upgraded.

requirements.title: Upgrading to the latest shape
requirements.statement: The schemas package shall export, for each format, a pure function that upgrades a decoded document of any shape to the latest shape, marking every fact the older version did not carry as `{ kind: "unknown" }` and never inventing a value.

requirements.title: Every document names its format and release
requirements.statement: phax shall write `$schema: "https://docs.phax.run/schemas/<format id>/<release version>.json"` as the first key of every persisted format it writes, taking the release version from its root `package.json`, and shall write no `version` literal in those formats.

requirements.title: Historical decoders are frozen
requirements.statement: The schemas package shall hold one decoder module per shape phax no longer writes — each format's pre-schema shape, and every released shape since — and a historical decoder shall not change once released. phax shall read a file it wrote in an older shape (its registry, a run's status) through those decoders and the format's `toLatest`, and shall refuse, naming the file and the fact, when a fact it needs comes back unknown.

requirements.title: A shape change is recorded as the next shape
requirements.statement: IF the JSON Schema generated for a format differs from that format's latest released snapshot and `<format id>/next.schema.json` does not equal it THEN phax's gate SHALL fail, naming the format and `<format id>/next.schema.json` as the snapshot to record.

requirements.title: The release names the next shapes
requirements.statement: WHEN `release.sh` cuts version X THE release script SHALL rename every `<format id>/next.schema.json` to `<format id>/X.schema.json` in the release commit.

requirements.title: Types match phax
requirements.statement: The schemas package shall ship TypeScript declarations whose type for each exported format is the type phax decodes that format to.

requirements.title: JSON Schema per format
requirements.statement: The schemas package shall ship one draft-07 JSON Schema file per exported format, generated at build time from the same schema that format's parse function uses.

requirements.title: No silent JSON Schema gap
requirements.statement: IF an exported format's JSON Schema cannot be generated THEN the schemas package build SHALL fail naming that format.

requirements.title: Lockstep version
requirements.statement: The schemas package shall be published at the same version as the phax release whose tag produced it.

requirements.title: Released with phax
requirements.statement: WHEN a release tag is pushed THE release workflow SHALL stage-publish the schemas package beside @lbdremy/phax.

requirements.title: All or nothing
requirements.statement: IF the schemas package build fails, or its packed tarball cannot be installed into an empty Node project and parse a phax-written document there, THEN the release workflow SHALL stage-publish neither package.

requirements.title: One release commit
requirements.statement: WHEN the release script bumps phax's version THE release script SHALL bump the schemas package manifest in the same release commit.

requirements.title: Code-review document when it ships
requirements.statement: WHERE a phax release carries the code-review document THE schemas package of that release SHALL export it like every other format.

nonGoals: The app and ports library API: exported use cases, adapter sets and a composition root. That work waits for 1.0 and the library-readiness item.

Exporting the phax.json or user-overlay config schemas. phax builds its effective config by merging layers, so decoding one file alone does not give the config phax would run with, and phax schema upgrade already delivers the JSON Schema for editors.

Writing the 1.0 stability contract itself (a frozen version plus a migration command, or a re-run-init policy). That stays with the Road to 1.0 item. This spec makes every shape readable; what 1.0 promises about changing shapes is that item's to say.
Any change to a persisted format's shape other than adding `$schema` and dropping `version`, or to the CLI. For the shape it writes, the package republishes what phax already enforces.
Reading helpers: nothing walks the records branch, finds run directories or reads files. The consumer reads the bytes and hands the package a JSON value.
Rewriting documents on disk. The package reads the pre-schema shape and every released shape and upgrades in memory; phax, the writer, writes only the latest version and keeps its no-shims rule.
A CommonJS build, a JSR or Deno-native publish, or JSON Schemas hosted at a URL. The docs pipeline reads the files from the installed package.
Parsing spec and plan Markdown frontmatter.

Exporting the internal formats listed in §5 (provider output streams, gate, reconciliation and session documents, extraction cache, orient, plan-audit, publication, security posture, telemetry events).

Reading documents older than a format's pre-schema shape (for example a version-1 phase record manifest). They are reported unsupported; the first supported release is the first that writes `$schema`.

acceptanceCriteria.name: A Node consumer parses a phase record end to end
acceptanceCriteria.given: an empty Node 20 project with no phax installed, in a repo whose phax/records/v1 branch holds a phase record.json written by phax
acceptanceCriteria.when: the packed @lbdremy/phax-schemas tarball is installed and the §6 consumer script runs with that record's <runId>/<phaseId> key
acceptanceCriteria.then: it prints the record's runId, phaseId and outcome and exits 0, and the project's node_modules holds only @lbdremy/phax-schemas, effect and effect's own dependencies

acceptanceCriteria.name: The package does no I/O
acceptanceCriteria.given: the packed @lbdremy/phax-schemas tarball
acceptanceCriteria.when: every JavaScript file it contains is scanned for imports and globals
acceptanceCriteria.then: none imports a node: built-in, fs, child_process or net, and none references Deno

acceptanceCriteria.name: The entry exports every persisted format
acceptanceCriteria.given: the installed package
acceptanceCriteria.when: the exports of @lbdremy/phax-schemas are listed
acceptanceCriteria.then: there is a schema, a type and a parse function for run registry, run status, phase status, phax-plan, compliance review, plan approvals, spec approvals, spec document, plan document, the phase and authoring record manifests, the record-manifest union, the gate attribution, the phase file reconciliation, the gate diagnostics and the gate pending document; the package has no other entry; none exists for an internal format

acceptanceCriteria.name: Nothing internal leaks
acceptanceCriteria.given: the packed @lbdremy/phax-schemas tarball
acceptanceCriteria.when: its file list and the exports of every entry are inspected
acceptanceCriteria.then: no export decodes a provider output stream, phax.json, the user overlay, a gate, reconciliation or session document, the extraction cache, or an orient or plan-audit response, and no file compiled from phax's app, ports, infra or cli layers is present

acceptanceCriteria.name: Same verdict as phax on every document
acceptanceCriteria.given: a corpus of accepted and rejected documents for every exported format, including a phase record.json with one unknown key and a registry.json with one unknown key
acceptanceCriteria.when: each document is parsed by the package's parse function and by phax's own decoder
acceptanceCriteria.then: the two verdicts agree on every document: the record with the unknown key is rejected by both, and the registry with the unknown key is accepted by both

acceptanceCriteria.name: A bad document is a value, not an exception
acceptanceCriteria.given: a run-status.json whose state is "paused"
acceptanceCriteria.when: parseRunStatus is called on its parsed JSON
acceptanceCriteria.then: it returns ok: false with error.path "state" and a non-empty error.message, and no exception escapes

acceptanceCriteria.name: Package types are phax's types
acceptanceCriteria.given: phax's type-test suite and the package's declarations
acceptanceCriteria.when: a value of each exported package type is assigned to phax's internal type for that format, and the reverse
acceptanceCriteria.then: both assignments typecheck for every exported format

acceptanceCriteria.name: Every exported format has a usable JSON Schema
acceptanceCriteria.given: the installed package and one phax-written document per exported format
acceptanceCriteria.when: each json/<format>.schema.json is loaded into a standard draft-07 validator and the matching document is validated
acceptanceCriteria.then: there is exactly one schema file per exported format and every phax-written document validates

acceptanceCriteria.name: A format without a JSON Schema fails the build
acceptanceCriteria.given: an exported format whose schema carries a refinement that has no JSON Schema rendering
acceptanceCriteria.when: the schemas package build runs
acceptanceCriteria.then: it exits non-zero naming that format, and the build output has no schema file for that format

acceptanceCriteria.name: Both packages are staged at the tag's version
acceptanceCriteria.given: a signed tag v0.17.0 on a commit whose release gate is green
acceptanceCriteria.when: the release workflow runs
acceptanceCriteria.then: @lbdremy/phax@0.17.0 and @lbdremy/phax-schemas@0.17.0 are both staged on npm

acceptanceCriteria.name: A broken package publishes nothing
acceptanceCriteria.given: a release commit whose schemas-package tarball fails to install into an empty Node project or fails to parse the smoke document
acceptanceCriteria.when: the release workflow runs on its tag
acceptanceCriteria.then: the workflow fails before any npm stage publish step runs, and neither package is staged

acceptanceCriteria.name: One commit bumps all manifests
acceptanceCriteria.given: a clean main at 0.16.0
acceptanceCriteria.when: scripts/release.sh 0.17.0 runs
acceptanceCriteria.then: the release commit sets version 0.17.0 in package.json, npm/package.json and the schemas package manifest, and the script's last lines name both staged packages

acceptanceCriteria.name: The code-review document joins like any format
acceptanceCriteria.given: a phax release that carries the code-review document
acceptanceCriteria.when: the exports of @lbdremy/phax-schemas and its json/ directory are listed
acceptanceCriteria.then: there is a code-review parse function and a code-review JSON Schema, on the same entry as every other format

acceptanceCriteria.name: Pre-schema and released shapes parse; older is unsupported
acceptanceCriteria.given: a phase record manifest in today's shape without `$schema` (version 2), one written with `$schema` by the first supported release, and a version-1 manifest from before `verifiedSurfaces` existed
acceptanceCriteria.when: each is given to parsePhaseRecordManifest
acceptanceCriteria.then: the first returns shape `pre-schema`, the second the shape of its release; the third returns a failure stating it is older than the first supported release and naming it, without throwing

acceptanceCriteria.name: A newer document is named
acceptanceCriteria.given: a phase record whose `$schema` names release 0.19.0, and a document whose `$schema` names an unknown format id
acceptanceCriteria.when: each is given to parseDocument
acceptanceCriteria.then: each returns a failure naming the URL and the package version and saying to upgrade the package, without throwing

acceptanceCriteria.name: Upgrading marks the unknown
acceptanceCriteria.given: a pre-schema phase record manifest
acceptanceCriteria.when: it is parsed and upgraded to the latest shape
acceptanceCriteria.then: the result has the latest shape; any fact the pre-schema shape lacks is `{ kind: "unknown" }`; every field it carried keeps its value

acceptanceCriteria.name: Every written document names its format and release
acceptanceCriteria.given: a phax built at 0.17.0
acceptanceCriteria.when: a run, an approval and a headless authoring session each write their documents
acceptanceCriteria.then: every document phax wrote starts with `$schema` set to `https://docs.phax.run/schemas/<its format id>/0.17.0.json` and carries no `version` key

acceptanceCriteria.name: phax imports only the current decoder
acceptanceCriteria.given: the built package and phax's source
acceptanceCriteria.when: their imports are inspected
acceptanceCriteria.then: phax's src/ imports no historical decoder module, and each historical module is byte-identical to its first released copy

acceptanceCriteria.name: A shape change must be recorded at its release
acceptanceCriteria.given: a change that adds a key to the phase record decoder, with no `phase-record-manifest/next.schema.json` yet
acceptanceCriteria.when: phax's gate runs
acceptanceCriteria.then: it fails naming the phase record and `phase-record-manifest/next.schema.json`; once that snapshot is written, it passes

acceptanceCriteria.name: A renamed file is still identified
acceptanceCriteria.given: a phase record written by phax 0.17.0, copied to `exports/a.json`, and an approvals ledger copied to `exports/b.json`
acceptanceCriteria.when: each is given to parseDocument
acceptanceCriteria.then: the first returns format `phase-record-manifest`, shape `0.17.0`; the second `plan-approvals`; no path is consulted

acceptanceCriteria.name: The release names the next shapes
acceptanceCriteria.given: `phase-record-manifest/next.schema.json` and `registry/next.schema.json` committed
acceptanceCriteria.when: scripts/release.sh 0.17.0 runs
acceptanceCriteria.then: the release commit renames them to `phase-record-manifest/0.17.0.schema.json` and `registry/0.17.0.schema.json`, and no `next` snapshot remains

acceptanceCriteria.name: phax reads its own older files through the package
acceptanceCriteria.given: a `~/.phax/registry.json` written by phax 0.16.0 (pre-schema, `version: 1`), and a phax at 0.17.0
acceptanceCriteria.when: `phax ls` runs, then any command that writes the registry
acceptanceCriteria.then: the runs are listed, read through the package's pre-schema decoder and `toLatest`; the rewritten registry starts with `$schema` naming `registry/0.17.0.json`; no phax module decodes the legacy shape itself

acceptanceCriteria.name: A record's timeline files parse
acceptanceCriteria.given: a record folder whose phase ran one diagnostics step twice — `record.json`, `gate-attribution.json`, `file-reconciliation.json`, `checks-attempt-01.diagnostics.json`, `checks-attempt-02.pending.json` — written by hand in the pre-schema shapes (no `version` on the four gate and reconciliation files)
acceptanceCriteria.when: each is given to its parse function
acceptanceCriteria.then: every call returns ok with shape `pre-schema`; the attempts' diagnostics are available in order, so the two fix-loop attempts can be shown

acceptanceCriteria.name: No real document is committed
acceptanceCriteria.given: the repository's test fixtures and the schemas package
acceptanceCriteria.when: they are inspected
acceptanceCriteria.then: every test document is written by hand or built from a schema; none is a copy of a document from a phax home, a records branch or another repository

openQuestions.question: Should the schemas ship as their own package or as a subpath of the existing @lbdremy/phax package?

options.label: A separate package, @lbdremy/phax-schemas
options.abandons: single-package releases: every release stages, approves and version-matches a second npm package.

options.label: A subpath, @lbdremy/phax/schemas
options.abandons: a lightweight dependency: every schema consumer installs the CLI launcher and its platform-binary resolution, and every CLI user installs effect.

openQuestions.rationale: Decided by the author on 2026-09-28, as recommended. The launcher and the library have disjoint audiences and dependencies. A second staged publish is one more step in a workflow that is already automated and approved by hand, which is a cost worth paying to keep the consumer's install small.

openQuestions.question: How should the package depend on effect?

options.label: A regular dependency on effect, with the same range as phax
options.abandons: a guaranteed single copy: a consumer pinned to an incompatible Effect version gets a second copy, and Schema values from the two copies do not compose.

options.label: A peer dependency on effect
options.abandons: a one-line install: a consumer that does not use Effect must add effect itself and match the range.

options.label: Bundle effect into the package
options.abandons: interoperability: the exported Schema values belong to a private copy of Effect, so an Effect consumer cannot compose them.

openQuestions.rationale: Decided by the author on 2026-09-28, as recommended. The first consumer is not assumed to use Effect. With a regular dependency, npm install @lbdremy/phax-schemas is the whole install, and package managers dedupe within ^3 for consumers that do use Effect.

openQuestions.question: What should a parse call return?

options.label: A plain Parsed result ({ ok, value } or { ok, error: { path, message } }), with the Effect schemas also exported
options.abandons: a single API: each format has both a parse wrapper and its schema, and they must stay in step.

options.label: Effect's Either<T, ParseError>, the decodeX functions phax uses internally
options.abandons: use without Effect: a non-Effect consumer must learn Either and how to format a ParseError before reading one field.

options.label: Return the value or throw
options.abandons: failures as values: a consumer walking many records has to wrap each call in try/catch to keep going.

openQuestions.rationale: Decided by the author on 2026-09-28, as recommended. The wrapper is generated from the same schema, so it can drift in spelling but not in verdict. Effect consumers still get the schemas directly, and non-Effect consumers get a result they can read without learning Effect.

openQuestions.question: Should parse functions reject unknown keys the way phax does?

options.label: Parity: each format keeps phax's own excess-property setting
options.abandons: forward compatibility: an older package rejects a record that a newer phax wrote with a new key, so the reader has to upgrade to match the writer.

options.label: Lenient: every parse function ignores unknown keys
options.abandons: the package's central claim: it would accept documents phax itself rejects, and a mistyped or foreign key would go unnoticed.

openQuestions.rationale: Decided by the author on 2026-09-28, as recommended. The package exists to be phax's decoder rather than a second one. Lockstep versioning makes the upgrade path explicit: a reader pins the package to the phax version that writes its files.

openQuestions.question: How should the package mark a format as experimental?

options.label: A separate experimental entry (@lbdremy/phax-schemas/experimental)
options.abandons: a stable import path across graduation: when a format becomes stable, its import line moves and every consumer must edit it.

options.label: A JSDoc @experimental tag on root-entry exports
options.abandons: visibility at the point of use: nothing in the import line or at compile time shows that a consumer depends on an experimental format.

openQuestions.rationale: Superseded on 2026-09-28 by q-no-experimental: with every shape readable through `$schema`, no format is marked stable or experimental. Decided by the author on 2026-09-28, as recommended. The import line is where a consumer takes on the dependency, so it is the right place to acknowledge the risk. A graduation that forces an edit is a feature, because the consumer sees the format change status.

openQuestions.question: While the 1.0 promise is still unwritten, should records, approvals and the compliance review be marked stable?

options.label: Stable: registry, run and phase status, phax-plan, compliance review, both approvals files and the phase record manifest
options.abandons: freedom to reshape the record manifest, the approvals files or the compliance review before 1.0 without bumping their version literal.

options.label: Experimental until the 1.0 promise is written
options.abandons: a stable footing for the first consumer: the cockpit would be built on formats phax says may change without notice.

openQuestions.rationale: Superseded on 2026-09-28 by q-no-experimental: with every shape readable through `$schema`, no format is marked stable or experimental. Decided by the author on 2026-09-28, as recommended. The promise draft in NEXT_STEPS already names approvals.json and phax/records/v1, and the README's 'run formats' covers the files in the run directory. The cockpit exists to read records. Stable already means only that a shape change bumps the version literal, and phax has done this before (the record manifest went from 1 to 2).

openQuestions.question: How should the package be versioned?

options.label: Lockstep: always the phax release version
options.abandons: meaningful version numbers: the package publishes new versions with no schema change, so a version bump does not signal a format change.

options.label: Independent semver that moves only when a format changes
options.abandons: the mapping from writer to reader: a consumer can no longer tell which package version reads the files a given phax release wrote.

openQuestions.rationale: Decided by the author on 2026-09-28, as recommended. The question a reader asks is which package reads what phax X.Y.Z wrote, and lockstep answers it with no lookup table. Extra releases with no change cost nothing to consume.

openQuestions.question: Does the package read only the version phax writes, or every version phax has ever written?

options.label: Every version ever written, each with its frozen decoder
options.abandons: a package that is only phax's current decoder: it carries historical decoders phax no longer runs

options.label: Only the version phax writes, like phax itself
options.abandons: reading history: the cockpit could not read the 6 version-1 phase records already on the records branch

openQuestions.rationale: Superseded on 2026-09-30 by q-support-start. Decided by the author on 2026-09-28. Git keeps every document phax ever wrote, and the first consumer reads that history, so every version stays readable. phax, the writer, keeps its no-shims rule.

openQuestions.question: What does a parse function return on a history that mixes versions?

options.label: The exact shape of the document's version, plus a pure toLatest that marks missing facts `unknown`
options.abandons: a single shape at the call site: the consumer upgrades explicitly

options.label: The exact shape only
options.abandons: a shared upgrade path: each consumer writes its own

options.label: Always the latest shape
options.abandons: the original shape, and honesty about absent facts, which must be given a value

openQuestions.rationale: Decided by the author on 2026-09-28, as recommended.

openQuestions.question: How does a document say which format it is and which phax release produced it?

options.label: A required `producedBy` field in every persisted format
options.abandons: unchanged formats: each format bumps its version once to add the field

options.label: A `Phax-Version` trailer on phax's commits
options.abandons: provenance for files never committed (run directory, registry), and a lookup of the commit for every document

options.label: Both
options.abandons: a single place: the trailer duplicates the field

options.label: One `$schema` URL per document, `https://docs.phax.run/schemas/<format id>/<release>.json`: format id and producing release together
options.abandons: a version marker independent of phax releases, and a URL host that must stay stable

openQuestions.rationale: Decided by the author on 2026-09-28, after a second look: a file name or location does not identify a format (renames, several files of one format, one schema for a set of files), so every document carries its format id, and the producing release goes in the same identifier. The `$schema` URL is the convention phax.json already follows, and editors and validators can resolve it once docs.phax.run serves the schemas.

openQuestions.question: Must experimental formats bump their version on every shape change too?

options.label: Yes: experimental means no promise that a shape lasts, not no version
options.abandons: changing an experimental shape freely under the same version

options.label: Only stable formats bump
options.abandons: a readable history for experimental formats

openQuestions.rationale: Superseded on 2026-09-28 by q-format-version: with the release in `$schema`, every shape change of every format, experimental included, is recorded by the snapshot gate at the release that makes it; no manual bump remains. The authoring record shows the cost of the old way: two shapes under version 1.

openQuestions.question: How is it guaranteed that no shape change escapes a bump and that the whole history stays readable?

options.label: Committed JSON Schema snapshots per version checked by the gate, and a history corpus parsed at every release
options.abandons: a lighter gate: two more checks and a committed corpus

options.label: The history corpus only
options.abandons: catching a forgotten bump before the release

options.label: A written rule checked in review
options.abandons: a mechanical guarantee — the rule that let the authoring record drift

openQuestions.rationale: Superseded on 2026-09-30 by q-support-start. Decided by the author on 2026-09-28, as recommended.

openQuestions.question: Where do the decoders of versions phax no longer writes live?

options.label: Frozen in the package, one module per version; phax imports only the current one
options.abandons: one home for every decoder: history lives beside the package, not in src/schemas

options.label: In phax, which keeps every decoder
options.abandons: a CLI free of dead code, and the no-shims pressure on the writer

openQuestions.rationale: Decided by the author on 2026-09-28, as recommended. Refined on 2026-09-28 (q-own-legacy): phax itself reads a file it wrote in an older shape through these decoders and `toLatest`.

openQuestions.question: With `$schema`, does each format keep its own `version` literal?

options.label: No: the release in `$schema` is the only version of a new document; the package maps releases to shapes
options.abandons: a per-format counter a human reads at a glance; legacy documents keep theirs

options.label: Keep `version` and bump it on every shape change, beside `$schema`
options.abandons: a single source: two version markers that can disagree, and a bump to remember

openQuestions.rationale: Decided by the author on 2026-09-28, as recommended.

openQuestions.question: Once every document names its shape and every shape stays readable, is there still a stable / experimental split?

options.label: No: one entry, every format; a format has shapes, not a stability class
options.abandons: a marking at the import that says 'this may change': every format now may change, and every change stays readable

options.label: Keep a separate experimental entry
options.abandons: one entry and one `parseDocument`; a split that no longer protects the reader from anything

openQuestions.rationale: Decided by the author on 2026-09-28: experimental meant a shape could change unannounced; once a document can always be parsed, the distinction is moot.

openQuestions.question: Which release does `$schema` name, and how is an unreleased shape named?

options.label: The root `package.json` version; an unreleased shape is the `next` snapshot, renamed by `release.sh`
options.abandons: a development build naming its own shape: it writes the last cut release, and its documents are not read before a release

options.label: A committed constant naming the upcoming release
options.abandons: a single version source: a third place a release must bump

openQuestions.rationale: Decided by the author on 2026-09-28: a schema is consumed only after it is published, so the release that cuts it names it.

openQuestions.question: How does phax read a file it wrote in an older shape (its registry, a run's status)?

options.label: Through the package's historical decoders and `toLatest`, refusing when a needed fact is unknown
options.abandons: a CLI that imports only its current decoders

options.label: A one-step lift of the previous `version` inside phax
options.abandons: a single read path: a second one beside the package

options.label: Refuse and name a migration command
options.abandons: an upgrade with no gesture

openQuestions.rationale: Decided by the author on 2026-09-28, as recommended.

openQuestions.question: Beyond its manifest, which files of a record does the package read?

options.label: The ones the cockpit's run timeline reads: gate attribution, file reconciliation, gate diagnostics and pending documents
options.abandons: technical files (agent binding, model resolution, orient brief, security posture) staying free to change without a published shape

options.label: Every JSON file of the folder
options.abandons: freedom over technical files nobody reads

options.label: The manifest only
options.abandons: the cockpit's timeline without a parser of its own — the reason the package exists

openQuestions.rationale: Decided by the author on 2026-09-29. A record is a folder, and the cockpit's first slice shows each phase's gate, fix loops and reconciliation, which live in those files.

openQuestions.question: What is the `record.json` format called?

options.label: `phase-record-manifest` / `authoring-record-manifest` (`parsePhaseRecordManifest`, …)
options.abandons: shorter names

options.label: `phase-record` / `authoring-record`
options.abandons: the distinction between a record (the folder) and its manifest (one file)

openQuestions.rationale: Decided by the author on 2026-09-29: "record" names the folder; its index file is the manifest.

openQuestions.question: From which document on does the package guarantee reading?

options.label: From the first release that writes `$schema`; a document without it is read by its format's pre-schema decoder (today's shape) or reported unsupported
options.abandons: the oldest documents (for example version-1 phase record manifests, early reconciliations): a handful of early runs show as unsupported

options.label: Every document ever written, through decoders built from a committed history corpus (the previous design)
options.abandons: a small, public-safe repository: over a thousand real documents committed, which leaked private runs on 2026-09-29

options.label: Reconstruct each release's schemas by checking out every phax version
options.abandons: a proportionate effort: a large tool to read documents the consumer can do without

openQuestions.rationale: Decided by the author on 2026-09-30. Today's decoders already accept the great majority of existing documents; the rest are early runs the cockpit can show as unsupported. The guarantee that matters starts now and holds forever.

settled: The Parsed result shape; Effect schemas and types are exported too.
Parity with phax's own decoders, including per-format excess-property handling.
effect is a regular dependency with the same range as phax.
The version is lockstep with phax, bumped by release.sh and published by the release workflow as a staged publish beside @lbdremy/phax.

Identification (2026-09-28): every document phax writes starts with `$schema: https://docs.phax.run/schemas/<format id>/<release>.json` and carries no `version`; `parseDocument` identifies a document by it alone; shapes are named by their release, plus one pre-schema shape per format; a shape change is recorded as a snapshot at its release by the gate.

Package name @lbdremy/phax-schemas: one entry carrying every persisted format (§5 list) and a json/ directory with one draft-07 JSON Schema per format, describing its latest shape; no stable/experimental split (q-no-experimental).
`$schema` names the root package.json version; unreleased shapes are `next` snapshots renamed by release.sh (q-release-name). phax reads its own older files through the package (q-own-legacy).

A record is a folder; its `record.json` is the manifest (`phase-record-manifest`, `authoring-record-manifest`). The package also reads the record's timeline files: gate attribution, phase file reconciliation, gate diagnostics and pending documents (2026-09-29).

Support starts at the first release that writes `$schema` (2026-09-30, q-support-start): each format has one pre-schema shape, today's, frozen when that release ships; older documents are unsupported. No history corpus, no survey-based decoders, no real document in the repository.
open: Where the package manifest and its entry modules live in the repo, and how its build is driven (a second tsc project over the same sources, or equivalent).
Spellings of parse functions, schema and type aliases and JSON Schema file names.
Whether the tarball install smoke also runs in pnpm check:full or only in the release workflow.
The exact URL path under docs.phax.run and the spelling of the unknown marker.
constraints: Build from the same src/schemas modules phax imports, with no copied schema. A change to a format must change the package in the same commit.

The entry closure reaches phaxConfig.ts (through runRecord's SurfaceSchema) and domain/branded.ts (through status's BranchNameSchema). Both must stay free of I/O, and vibeOutput.ts (node:fs) must be unreachable from any entry. An architectural guard should enforce this closure.
No persisted format changes shape, phax's own decoding is unchanged, and the CLI does not change. The no-shims policy holds.
In the release workflow, every step that can fail runs before the first npm stage publish. The hand-approval step now covers two packages.
knip must treat the package entries as public entry points, so it does not flag their exports as unused.
With approvals files versioned, artifact-decide's unattributed approvals need no rewrite of history: phax migrates the live ledger, and the package reads older ledger versions as they are.

Several Approved specs change formats this package exports (oracle-phases, artifact-decide, headless-review). Whatever lands in one release forms one shape at that release: its snapshot is rewritten until the release is cut, never after.
The `$schema` URLs must resolve: the docs.phax.run release pipeline (NEXT_STEPS) serves every release's schema of every format at `/schemas/<format id>/<release>.json`, and never removes one.
The code-review document joins the package in the release that ships the headless-review spec, not before.

docsPage.page: README.md §"Read phax files from code" (a section beside the persisted-formats table)
docsPage.reader: Someone writing a tool, such as a dashboard, a cockpit or a docs pipeline, that reads phax's registry, run files, approvals or records and wants phax's own types and verdicts instead of a hand-written parser.
docsPage.example: npm install @lbdremy/phax-schemas, then the §6 read-record.mjs script: git show phax/records/v1:<runId>/phase-01/record.json, parsePhaseRecordManifest(JSON.parse(raw)), branch on parsed.ok, then read parsed.value.outcome. It ends with a pointer to json/<format>.schema.json for docs tooling and a note that every document stays readable: an older shape parses, a newer release asks to upgrade the package.
